components.cost_effect: One product per update reused in the residual recurrence; direction formation adds vector arithmetic but no further matrix product.
components.goal: Generate mutually A-conjugate directions without storing the full direction history.
components.key_estimate: Distinct nonzero residuals are orthogonal and generated nonzero directions are pairwise A-conjugate; see linked batch Theorem.
components.name: Residual and conjugate-direction recurrence
components.operation: Form the next direction from the new residual plus b_i times the preceding direction.
components.requires: Real SPD matrix and exact arithmetic; continue only with a nonzero residual.
transfer_checks: For nonsymmetric/indefinite A, inexact products, finite precision, preconditioning or altered inner products, re-establish denominator positivity and all orthogonality invariants.

content.family: Unpreconditioned Conjugate Gradient, a Conjugate Directions method.

limitations.statement: The finite-termination statement does not apply to rounded or inexact recurrences; the source explicitly discusses failure to reach the exact solution after n rounded steps.
This record makes no lower-bound or optimality claim for unrestricted matrix-vector-product algorithms and no tolerance-dependent floating-point rate claim.

performance_links.scope_note: At most n exact-arithmetic updates with exact zero-residual output; initialization product and other arithmetic are separately charged.

variants.cost: Implementation accounting of the displayed recurrence: one Ax_0 initialization product, unless its value is already known (e.g. x_0=0), then exactly one A p_i per update. Cache rho_i: one initial residual squared-norm inner product; each update has one (p_i,A p_i) inner product and one new residual squared-norm inner product. Each update separately requires two vector scaled additions for x and r, and each continued update one for the next p; scalar divisions for a_i and, when continuing, b_i are additional arithmetic. O(n) working vector storage excluding representation/storage of A and its product implementation. Matrix-vector product arithmetic cost depends on that representation and is not treated as free.
variants.implementation_details_ref: §3 p.411 Eq(3:1a–f) and routine description; §5 p.414 Eq(5:1a–f). Zero-residual guards and caching are explicit implementation conventions preserving the original exact-arithmetic sequence.
variants.name: Real SPD exact-arithmetic CG
variants.output: The first x_m with r_m=0, including x_0 when initially solved; then Ax_m=k.
public_inputs: Known k in R^n and arbitrary x_0 in R^n
Access to exact v -> A v, with A a real n-by-n SPD matrix
variants.query_and_update: For i=0,1,... while r_i != 0, query q_i=A p_i; set rho_i=(r_i,r_i), a_i=rho_i/(p_i,q_i), x_{i+1}=x_i+a_i p_i, r_{i+1}=r_i-a_i q_i. If r_{i+1}=0 return x_{i+1}; otherwise b_i=(r_{i+1},r_{i+1})/rho_i and p_{i+1}=r_{i+1}+b_i p_i. Reuse q_i in both denominator and residual update.
variants.requirements: Real SPD A, Euclidean inner products, exact arithmetic and exact matrix-vector products. Right-hand side k is known. No eigenvalue estimate, condition-number estimate, preconditioner or sampling is required.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set r_0=k-Ax_0 and p_0=r_0. If r_0=0, return x_0 without entering the recurrence. Store x,r,p and a reusable product buffer.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: No free step-size or accuracy parameter: a_i and b_i are determined by the recurrence. Test the exact zero residual before any division at the next iteration; return on the first zero residual. The linked Theorem bounds updates by n. This is not a floating-point tolerance prescription.
